input.quote: the matter shall be referred to the Management Committee which shall either resolve the matter or determine the method, such as arbitration, by which the matter should be resolved. This procedure shall be the sole and exclusive remedy for any dispute which may arise under this Agreement between or among the Parties.
input.rationale: The Agreement designates no governing law at all (Para 27.2 only excludes certain facts from a later choice-of-law determination, and Paras 20 and 25 merely reference the law of the arbitration/litigation forum and general legal compliance), and its only dispute forum is a Management Committee that may itself "determine the method, such as arbitration" as the "sole and exclusive remedy" - an open-ended, potentially foreign-seated arbitral route with no court venue. That fails the fallback (Delaware/California courts or England and Wales with the courts of London) on both material terms and approaches walk-away territory. We therefore replaced the committee-determined exclusive remedy with the preferred position: New York law and exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County, retaining the Committee as a resolution step and leaving 27.1's continued-performance sentence and 27.2 untouched.

mappings.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.

proposal.summary: Add New York governing law and exclusive New York County court jurisdiction in place of the committee-determined (potentially arbitral) sole and exclusive remedy.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement designates no governing law and makes a Management Committee determination (possibly arbitration with no stated seat) the sole and exclusive remedy, so we have replaced that mechanic with New York law and exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County, keeping the Committee as a resolution step. Delaware, California, or England and Wales with the courts of London would also work for us.
